previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a patient with a history of cholangiocarcinoma and biliary stents, was admitted with fever, nausea, and vomiting. Workup revealed multifocal cholangitis and partial stent obstruction on MRCP. He was started on IV meropenem for suspected biliary infection. During ERCP to clear the stent, he developed hemobilia which resolved spontaneously without intervention. He remained hemodynamically stable, afebrile, and improved clinically. His pancytopenia remained stable throughout. He completed a 7-day course of antibiotics and was discharged home in stable condition with follow-up planned with gastroenterology and oncology.

EXAMINATION:  MRCP

INDICATION:  ___ year old man with cholangiocarcinoma, recurrent biliary
obstruction/cholangitis s/p stenting p/w fevers.// biliary obstruction?
evidence of cholangitis?

TECHNIQUE:  T1- and T2-weighted multiplanar images of the abdomen were
acquired in a 1.5 T magnet.
Intravenous contrast: 8 mL Gadavist.
Oral contrast:  1 cc of Gadavist mixed with 50 cc of water was administered
for oral contrast.

COMPARISON:  MRCP from ___

FINDINGS: 

Lower Thorax: Atelectatic changes are present in both lung bases.

Liver: There are multifocal patchy areas of parenchymal T2 hyperintensity and
arterial hyperenhancement in the right hepatic lobe, in the same distribution
as on the previous study involving segments 5 and 6, compatible with
cholangitis.  The extent of the parenchymal signal abnormality is however
decreased compared to previous.  There is no intrahepatic abscess.

Re-demonstration of an ill-defined T1 hypointense area at the confluence of
the hepatic ducts, which demonstrates arterial enhancement without washout,
appearing stable to previous.  There is persistent mild intrahepatic biliary
duct dilatation, left greater than right, unchanged since the previous study. 
Unchanged left hepatic lobe atrophy.  2 common duct stents are present, in
unchanged position.

Pancreas: The pancreas is normal in signal intensity and morphology.  There is
no pancreatic ductal dilatation.

Spleen: The spleen is enlarged measuring up to 17 cm.

Adrenal Glands: The bilateral adrenal glands are unremarkable.

Kidneys: Re-demonstration of a simple appearing cyst at the lower pole of the
left kidney.  Tiny cortical cyst in the interpolar region of the right kidney.
There is no hydronephrosis.

Gastrointestinal Tract:  Visualized bowel loops are unremarkable, without
evidence of obstruction.

Lymph Nodes: No retroperitoneal or mesenteric lymphadenopathy.

Vasculature: Persistent, severe attenuation of both the right and left portal
veins.

Osseous and Soft Tissue Structures: Unremarkable.

IMPRESSION: 

Persistent, although decreased cholangitis in the right hepatic lobe,
involving segments 5 and 6.  No evidence of intrahepatic abscess.

Stable mild intrahepatic biliary duct dilatation, left greater than right. 
Persistent abnormal parenchymal signal with enhancement at the confluence of
the hepatic ducts, likely related to posttreatment inflammatory fibrosis. 
Underlying viable tumor cannot be excluded.
